newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: British pressure group opposes wider rhino trade.
newsitem.headline: British pressure group opposes wider rhino trade.

text.p: A British-based environmental watchdog on Monday urged rejection of a proposal by South Africa to allow trade in white rhinoceros parts.

TRAFFIC (Trade Records Analysis of Flora and Fauna in Commerce) said in its recommendations to the 10-day Convention on Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) that Pretoria's proposal was premature because there was concern in South Africa itself that there were inadequate controls to monitor trade.
Trade in South Africa's white rhinoceroses is currently restricted to live animals and sport-hunted trophies.
TRAFFIC hailed as a remarkable achievement South Africa's record in conservation of black and white African rhinoceroses.
But South Africa was seeking support for an investigation of the possibility of bilateral trade in rhino products to earn funds for conservation and to reduce incentives for illegal trade.
"The proposal to broaden the current annotation to include the possibility of trade in rhinoceros parts and derivatives (initially subject to a zero quota) is premature at this time," TRAFFIC said.
Mechanisms to collect data and evaluate the effectiveness of current policies were not yet in place, it said.
